<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/automation.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in ApiTriggerSignatureSchema))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in ApiTriggerSignatureSchema))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const), invalid_type (literal, a string literal in ApiTriggerSignatureSchema))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in ApiTriggerSignatureSchema))_
- `content/docs/frontend/cli.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in ApiTriggerSignatureSchema), invalid_union (literal, a string literal in ApiTriggerSignatureSchema))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in ApiTriggerSignatureSchema))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const), invalid_type (literal, a string literal in ApiTriggerSignatureSchema), invalid_union (literal, a string literal in ApiTriggerSignatureSchema))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in ApiTriggerSignatureSchema))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/automation.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **169** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `adf2277cafc8afea75fb04491686ea06f89119a9` — the merge of head `bb371a5c3103db11490cb2cc4c39c378b588a755` into base `0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin adf2277cafc8afea75fb04491686ea06f89119a9 && git checkout adf2277cafc8afea75fb04491686ea06f89119a9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76 bb371a5c3103db11490cb2cc4c39c378b588a755 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76 && git merge --no-ff bb371a5c3103db11490cb2cc4c39c378b588a755

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `db0c0f86b017b8d0400c2571277e46fc38a40b89`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/api-trigger-signature.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/trigger-api-service.ts + packages/spec/src/automation/api-trigger-signature.test.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/api-trigger-secret-ref.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/index.ts, packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts, .changeset/29983-api-trigger-signature.md, the eight ledgers (api-surface, authorable-surface, declaration-map, export-origins, json-schema.manifest, llms.txt, variant-docs.json, strictness ledger + counts), skills/objectstack-automation/references/_index.md, and on main: packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/api-trigger.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/plugin.ts, packages/core/src/security/http-signature.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts, packages/spec/scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts, packages/spec/liveness/flow.json, scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-references.ts, docs/adr/0138 D7/F1, docs/adr/0041 Tier 1.

### ① Derived judgments

- Exports: `ApiTriggerSignatureSchema` (discriminated union on `signs`), its two arms `ApiTriggerBodySignatureSchema` / `ApiTriggerTimestampedSignatureSchema` (both `strictObject`, `history` BORN_CLOSED), aliases `ApiTriggerSignature` / `ApiTriggerBodySignature` / `ApiTriggerTimestampedSignature` (`z.input`, three ADR-0122 Iso pins, count 828 to 831 with the recomputed-count assertion moved), `API_TRIGGER_SIGNATURE_KEY`, `ApiTriggerVerifier`, `ApiTriggerSignatureRefusal`, `apiTriggerVerifierOf`, `apiTriggerSignatureRefusals`. Each lands in api-surface, export-origins (12 entries, same spelling), declaration-map (6 names to 3 defs) and the json-schema manifest (3 defs; `packages/spec/json-schema/` is gitignored, so the manifest is the committed half). Right.
- Accept-set: `flow.nodes[].config` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (flow.zod.ts:699); the new key is judged by a `superRefine` walk (`apiTriggerSignatureRefusals`) placed beside the `secretRef` walk at 1700. A flow with no `signature` key parses exactly as before (pinned). Widening, with the key born closed.
- authorable-surface: 11 rows (5 body-arm keys, 6 timestamped-arm keys); exporting the arms as defs is what makes the surface move, since the union def has no `properties`. Right.
- llms.txt 217 to 218 / automation 15 to 16; references index 15 to 16 pages, 78 to 81 schemas, 1620 to 1623; `meta.json` ordering under More. Consistent with three new defs in one new module.
- Strictness ledger: counts +2 sites (the two `strictObject` calls), one hand row `authorable`, strict from birth, naming the open `config` slot and why the open-slot exemption does not extend to it. Right.
- variant-docs.json: `signs:body|timestamp.body` entered `exempt: generated-reference-only` with a reason that names the server slice as the binder of the flows.mdx section. Acceptable for a key no trigger serves; the slice must replace it.
- skills/objectstack-automation/references/_index.md: generated. `build-skill-references.ts` closes over flow.zod.ts's imports (Transitive dependencies) and writes the module doc block's first line, which is byte-equal to the header line in the new module. The #11705 carve-out (`check-governed-merges.mjs` row `generator: pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:skill-refs`) lifts it only on a byte-exact `check:skill-refs`; `Lint · scoped` was still running at read time. No hand-authored `skills/**` content moves.
- Liveness: the claim "no `planned` + `authorWarn` row is reachable under `config`" is measured true: `childShape` answers a record by `shapeOf(def.valueType)`, and `z.unknown()` has no shape (check-liveness.mts:669); flow.json's own `_note` records the same refusal for `excludeSubmitter` (`declared children but property is not a container`). The sibling `secretRef` has no row for the same reason. Nothing is missing from the ledgers.
- Not moved, correctly: `packages/triggers/trigger-api`, `@objectstack/core`, the error-code ledger (`INVALID_SIGNATURE` row unchanged), the lint readiness rule.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/29983-api-trigger-signature.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; `Metadata-protocol: added`; ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` in the documented `<!-- adr-0087: ... -->` form with a why. Both lines match the PR body and the claim. Correct: a new optional key under an open record with no stored shape to rewrite and no migration prescription in the body (the gate's `no-migration-prescription` test is statement-against-statement). Same declarations as the `secretRef` precedent in packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md.
- The changeset's last paragraph states the dormant-key truth (declared, not verified, refuses every vendor post 401, admits none unverified). Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- os-dev-report 6619577200: `closing_keyword: Part of #29983` is the right choice; the card's need is met only by the `domain:server` slice, so the card must stay open. `fork_reported: false`, `security_findings: none filed`, deviations enumerated (liveness, metadata-form, no people on the PR). Gates 107/107/0 as reported; check-runs on the head at read time: no red, many still in progress.
- PR body flags: `Clause-②`, `Metadata-protocol`, `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` naming three skills lines and the flows.mdx section for the server slice, `ADR-0087`, prior rulings read (ADR-0138 D7/F1, ADR-0041 Tier 1, ruling B on #22805). The D7 reading is right: D7 left the vocabulary out of `ApiEndpointSchema` and F1 filed it "with its executor"; this PR has no executor yet, which the body states and the changeset states.
- Server-slice checklist is coherent with main: today only `x-objectstack-signature` and `x-idempotency-key` reach `handleRequest` (plugin.ts:99-100), so the header pass-through item is real; `start()` refuses a secretless binding before arming, so the "refuse to arm as the missing-secret case does" option exists; `request.text()` on both faces, so the UTF-8 note is right.
- Draft, not auto-merged, Tier H by `skills/**` and by the human floor (maintainer reviews the contract). Right.

### ④ Design judgment

- Single verifier: `apiTriggerVerifierOf` decides on key PRESENCE (`hasOwnProperty`), so a present-and-broken `signature` is `unusable`, never `objectstack-signature`; the arms are strict so `optional` / `fallback` / `also` are refused on both (pinned). Neither-runs is unreachable; both-optional is unreachable. Holds.
- Key: `signature` with no `secretRef` refused; beside `secret` (including `''`) refused; `secretRef` present but unusable (`OS_` prefix) is `unusable` at the reader and refused at the `secretRef` walk. On main, `flow-definitions.ts` returns the resolver for `secretRef` before it ever consults the write-only store, so the store cannot become a second key. Holds.
- Closed sets: `algorithm` one value, `encoding` two values, `signs` two literals; parse refusals pinned at `.algorithm`, `.encoding`, `.signs`, `.header`, `.prefix`, `.timestampElement`, `.digestElement`, all `code: 'custom'` at `nodes.N.config.signature...`. Holds.
- Replay: `timestamp.body` requires `timestampElement` and `digestElement` (distinct); the contract makes the window mandatory and names `HTTP_SIGNATURE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS` (300, both directions, `Math.abs` today), applied after the HMAC verifies, as `verifyHttpSignature` does. `body` states "no replay window applies to it: a captured post verifies again for as long as the key is unchanged", and refuses a timestamp element on that arm. Holds.
- Prefix and lists: `prefix` only on the body arm, required on the wire when declared ("a value without it fails"); timestamped arm locates by `digestElement`, one or more (`v1=a,v1=b` any one matching admits; a repeated `t` fails; unknown elements ignored; split at the first `=`, so base64 padding survives). Holds.
- One answer: every step of a declared scheme answers the same `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` one body; cause to the server log only (`refuseUnverified` today). Constant-time compare of the decoded 32 bytes is stated in bold, with the 32-byte length rule. No contract string carries a key, a digest or a body. Holds.
- Fit: DocuSign Connect (base64 HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body in `X-DocuSign-Signature-1`), Stripe-style (`t=…,v1=…` hex over `<t>.<raw body>`, 300 s), GitHub-style (`sha256=` hex) each parse whole and are served as written (pinned).
- MUST-FIX (header collision with the platform's own header): `HTTP_FIELD_NAME` admits `header: 'x-objectstack-signature'` in any case. `{ signs: 'body', header: 'X-Objectstack-Signature', encoding: 'hex', prefix: 'sha256=' }` parses, keyed by `secretRef`, and makes the hook admit exactly the body-only `sha256=` form of the platform's own header that ruling B on #22805 refuses inbound because it signs no time, while ObjectStack's own senders offer the timestamped form (`signHttpBodyAt`): a replay bound the sender offers is dropped by configuration, against the triage floor. It also makes the contract sentence "it never reads `x-objectstack-signature`" false by construction. Fix in this PR: a second `.regex` on `header` (so the JSON Schema carries it) refusing that name without regard to case, one pin in the test, one line in the module header's refusal list.
- SHOULD-FIX (headers the contract promises not to read): the same regex admits `authorization`, `cookie`, `proxy-authorization`, `host`, `content-length`, `transfer-encoding` and the door's own `x-idempotency-key`. All fail closed, but `authorization` and `cookie` contradict "This member ... reads no session, cookie or `Authorization` header". Refuse a closed list at parse, or state in the contract that a declared header is read as an opaque signature value whatever its name.
- SHOULD-FIX (repeated header): `Headers.get` joins repeated fields with `, `; the contract should say the joined string is the one value (fails to decode for `body`; a doubled `t` is "repeated" for `timestamp.body`) so no implementer reads the first field alone.
- SHOULD-FIX (the `unusable` answer): "admits no post at all" names no status. Pin it to the one `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` whether the trigger refuses to arm (then `unknown-flow`) or refuses each post, so a misdeclared hook never shows a 5xx or a second body.
- SHOULD-FIX (readiness): `validate-flow-trigger-readiness` grades a `secretRef` + `signature` hook ready today while no trigger serves the key; the server checklist lists the readiness note as "optionally". Make it a required item of that slice (or add the warn now), so an author is told before the slice lands.

## Contract review — delta (fix round 1)

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4194519e9650f9b41cafb1fa8ad64e6d8c03a0b1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/api-trigger-signature.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/api-trigger-signature.test.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/trigger-api-service.ts, .changeset/29983-api-trigger-signature.md, packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json, packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json, content/docs/references/automation/api-trigger-signature.mdx (the seven files the delta touches) + the net diff for packages/spec/declaration-map/automation.json, packages/spec/llms.txt, packages/spec/json-schema.manifest/automation.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json; the proposed body /mnt/project-files/seat3-orders/29983-body-r1.md; scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs (Rules 2 and 3), scripts/pm/check-skill-id-lint.mjs (roots); on main: packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/plugin.ts:62-100, packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/api-trigger.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-api/package.json (hono ^4.13.9).

### ① Derived judgments

- MUST-FIX (platform header) — closed and pinned. `reservedHeaderMessage` lower-cases the parsed `header` and refuses `x-objectstack-signature` at `nodes.N.config.signature.header`; the lookup runs only after `HTTP_FIELD_NAME` (ASCII token) has passed, so no Unicode case-fold (Kelvin sign and the like) can reach the set. Pinned in three spellings (lower, Title, UPPER) on both arms (GITHUB_STYLE body with `sha256=`, STRIPE_STYLE timestamped), each read `unusable` by `apiTriggerVerifierOf`. Ablation is visible: `refusalsUnderSignature` asserts `success === false` and the exact path list, so a refusal that answers nothing, or one that drops the case fold, goes red. Delivered as a post-parse refusal in the shared `signatureConfigRefusals` walk rather than the `.regex` the prior review named; see ④ for the one consequence.
- SHOULD-FIX 1 (reserved list) — closed and pinned. `API_TRIGGER_SIGNATURE_RESERVED_HEADERS` is `Object.freeze([...] as const)`, exported, pinned whole by value and `Object.isFrozen`; each name after the first is refused in three spellings on the body arm with its own message; near names (`X-Objectstack-Signature-1`, `X-Authorization-Signature`, `Signature`, `X-Cookie-Sig`) still parse. The list is right for what it guards: the declaration only chooses which field's value is HMAC-verified under the hook's key, so no header choice weakens the check and nothing an attacker controls is admitted by it; `x-forwarded-*`, `x-real-ip`, hop-by-hop fields and the platform's outbound `x-objectstack-delivery` / `-event` / `-attempt` would merely fail closed when a proxy rewrites or strips them, which is an author foot-gun, not an exposure. The eight names are exactly the ones the contract already promises not to read or reads for its own purpose (plugin.ts:99-100 reads only `x-objectstack-signature` and `x-idempotency-key`). Nothing wrongly included.
- SHOULD-FIX 2 (repeated header) — closed. Contract: one value, joined with `, ` in order received, "what `Headers.get` answers", never first or last alone; a repeated body-only header fails (the joined value cannot decode to 32 bytes, prefix or not); a repeated `t` is "repeated" on the timestamped arm. Matches both faces on main: `requestDoorContext.header` is `request.headers.get(name)` (plugin.ts:68) and Hono 4's `c.req.header(name)` is the same `Headers.get` read (plugin.ts:62 documents it). Changeset and body carry the same sentence.
- SHOULD-FIX 3 (`unusable` status) — closed. Contract, `ApiTriggerVerifier` JSDoc, changeset and body all name the one `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE`, "whether the trigger declines to arm the declaration or refuses each post"; coherent with `start()` refusing to arm (then unknown-flow is already that same 401). Contract text, so no runtime pin applies; the reader's `unusable` answer is pinned on every refused shape.
- SHOULD-FIX 4 (readiness) — closed in the body: the server-slice item now reads "`validate-flow-trigger-readiness` (required)" with the three obligations (not ready while unserved; grade names the verifier; `unusable` never ready).
- Ledgers: api-surface and export-origins each gain the one `(const)` row; declaration-map, json-schema.manifest, authorable-surface and llms.txt do not track consts (the sibling `API_TRIGGER_SECRET_REF_RESERVED_PREFIX` is absent from all four on main), so none should move and none did. The `header` `.describe()` change re-projected into the generated reference page, both arms, four tables. Nothing missing.
- Check-runs on the head at read time: 21 completed (success or skipped), none failed; still in progress: Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, two Lint · scoped shards, the four Type Check jobs, Build Core/Docs/UI Deps, Plan Test Core shards, Live E2E UI. PR-body guards, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness: success.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged and still right: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, ADR-0087 marker as before. The delta adds one exported frozen const and narrows the accept-set of a key born in this same release (a reserved `header` now refused), so no consumer on a published version is broken. The changeset's export list and refusal list were updated to name the const and the reserved-header refusal; the "repeated header" and "unusable 401" obligations were added to its contract sentence. Body and changeset agree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Proposed body: `Clause-②`, `Metadata-protocol`, `Skills-docs: follow-up owed`, `Prior rulings read`, `ADR-0087` lines unchanged; the 维护者速读 counts "六类拒绝含保留头名"; Acceptance notes add "Since contract review round 1, a declaration cannot re-admit that form on the platform's own header". Tests paragraph claims 25 cases (22 `it` + one 3-row `it.each`, consistent) and states the ablation. Verification is the stated placeholder; not counted.
- Refusal-message leaks: both new messages interpolate only the author's own `header` string; no key, digest or body. The reserved-header message names no tracker id; pinned negatively (`not.toMatch(/#\d/)`) on both messages. The sanctioned `//` comment holds the id (check-doc-authoring Rule 3's prescribed home).
- No earlier guarantee weakened: `apiTriggerVerifierOf` still decides on key presence; `unusable` still never falls back; the `secret`/`secretRef` refusals are untouched (the reserved check is added inside the `else` of a successful parse, and the same-element check moved into it unchanged).

### ④ Design judgment

- Single verifier, key by reference, closed sets, replay rule, one answer: all hold as before; the delta only narrows `header`.
- The doc-authoring fix: the reworded `x-objectstack-signature` message is accurate for the body arm and actionable on both ("Remove `signature` to verify `x-objectstack-signature`, or name the header the sender writes its own signature in"). SHOULD-FIX (low): its stated reason is arm-blind. For a `signs: 'timestamp.body'` declaration on that header the sentence "a declared scheme on it would re-admit that refused form, with no replay bound" is false (that arm has a bound); the true reason there is the one-verifier rule ("a hook that declares its sender's scheme never reads that header"), which the message does state first. Lead with the arm-neutral reason, or branch on `signs`.
- SHOULD-FIX (schema vs walk): the `header` `.describe()` now says "A reserved name is refused", and that text projects into the JSON Schema and the four reference tables, but `ApiTriggerSignatureSchema` itself admits a reserved name; only `signatureConfigRefusals` (hence `FlowSchema` and `apiTriggerVerifierOf`) refuses it.
